newsitem.title: USA: Microsensors next step in PC revolution - futurist.
newsitem.headline: Microsensors next step in PC revolution - futurist.

text.p: Cheap sensors that can hear and see the world will bring about the next revolution in computers, a prominent futurist said.

So-called micro electrical-mechanical systems, or MEMS, will give computers the ability to sense the world around them and manipulate their environment, said Paul Saffo, director of the Institute for the Future, a Silicon Valley think tank.
"Computers, which live in the digital world, have no clue that our analog world exists," Saffo said. Micro- sensors "will give them the ability to sense this world."
MEMS could first appear in something as simple as car airbags, where they can sense the size of the passenger and moderate the airbag explosion if the passenger is a child, Saffo said.
MEMS also will come in the form of video cameras that cost pennies, which would give computers vision.
The technology could have an impact on the computer industry just as profound as the microprocessor or the laser, Saffo said.
Saffo gave his presentation late Tuesday at the Millennium Conference in San Francisco, where several computer chief executives gave their predictions about how technology will change people's lives.

Saffo gave examples of several devices that already use MEMS, including skis that change their shapes to glide more smoothly. With MEMS, "smart" violins could be manufactured that would make the unsteady bowing of a beginner sound like a master's.
